mainTopic: Three women and blood in one bed, searching for hidden טומאה, and the stories and lessons that follow (נדה 61a)
overview: The amud opens with the last words of the previous discussion. Then a new משנה begins: three women sleep in one bed by a wall, and blood is found under one of them. Where the blood was found, how the women got into the bed, and which women examined themselves decide who is טמאה. The משנה compares this to a טמא pile of stones mixed up with two טהור piles. רבי מאיר says that if all the piles are searched and nothing is found, they all stay טמא. The חכמים say a search down to bedrock or untouched soil clears them. The גמרא explains why the רבנן still keep all three women טמאות: blood had to come from someone, while a raven might have carried off the טומאה from a pile. Stories follow about searches that missed hidden bones, and one clever search with wet sheets that found a pit full of bones. That pit leads to גדליה, who ignored a warning, and to רבא's rule that you must not believe לשון הרע but must still take precautions because of it. רבי טרפון applies this rule. The גמרא also explains why משה feared עוג but not סיחון. The amud ends with a ברייתא about a garment whose stain can no longer be found, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing words: treat them as if they could be the source
steps.stepSummary: The previous discussion ends by saying the women are viewed as if they were fit to have produced the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: As though they were fit.
steps.whatsHappening: This short line is the end of the previous discussion. The women in that case are treated as if they could have been the source of the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some women might seem unlikely to have produced the blood. Even so, they are not excluded. They are treated as possible sources, so they are טמאות along with the others.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit or capable, here meaning able to have been the source of the blood

phrases.english: as though they were fit.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from before this section: the women count as possible sources of the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּאִילּוּ הֵן רְאוּיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion that came before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Women who might seem unlikely sources are still treated as possible sources of the blood, so they are טמאות.

steps.title: Three women in one bed: where the blood is found decides who is impure
steps.stepSummary: Blood under the middle woman makes all three טמאות. Blood under an end woman makes her and her neighbor טמאות, and the far woman stays טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three women were sleeping in one bed, and blood was found under the middle one: all of them are טמאות. If it was found under the inner one, the two inner women are טמאות and the outer one is טהורה. If it was found under the outer one, the two outer women are טמאות and the inner one is טהורה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on which of three women in one bed become טמאות, based on where the blood was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood could have come from the woman it was found under, or from a woman right next to her. Blood under the middle woman is next to everyone, so all three are טמאות. Blood under an end woman cannot reach the woman on the far end, so she stays טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the base text being learned
The inner one (near the wall) / the outer one (far from the wall)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume only the woman the blood was found under is טמאה. Her neighbor could also be the source, so she is טמאה too.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלֹשׁ נָשִׁים שֶׁהָיוּ יְשֵׁנוֹת בְּמִטָּה אַחַת,
phrases.english: Three women who were sleeping in one bed,
and blood was found beneath the middle one —
all of them are impure.
Beneath the inner one —
the two inner ones are impure,
and the outer one is pure.
Beneath the outer one —
the two outer ones are impure,
and the inner one is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁלֹשׁ נָשִׁים שֶׁהָיוּ יְשֵׁנוֹת בְּמִטָּה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood under the middle woman makes all three טמאות. Blood under an end woman makes the two nearest women טמאות and leaves the far woman טהורה.

steps.title: The rule depends on how the women got into the bed
steps.stepSummary: The previous rules apply only if the women entered from the foot of the bed. If they climbed in over the bed itself, all three are טמאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this so? When they passed in by way of the foot of the bed. But if they passed over the bed itself, all of them are טמאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a condition that limits the rules it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each woman came in from the foot of the bed, only the women near the spot were ever over the blood. If they climbed across the bed, each of them passed over the spot where the blood was found. So any of them could have left it, and all three are טמאות.

keyTerms.meaning: When? It introduces a limit on a rule
By way of the bed itself, crossing over it

phrases.english: When?
At a time when they passed via the foot of the bed,
but if they passed over it —
phrases.notes: They climbed across the bed, over the spot where the blood was later found.

phrases.english: all of them are impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָתַי בִּזְמַן שֶׁעָבְרוּ דֶּרֶךְ מַרְגְּלוֹת הַמִּטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rules of step 2 to one way of entering the bed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rules about who stays טהורה apply only if the women entered from the foot of the bed. If they crossed over the bed, all three are טמאות.

steps.title: What a self-examination does
steps.stepSummary: A woman who examines herself and is found clean becomes טהורה, and the others stay טמאות. If all three are found clean, all three are טמאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of them examined herself and was found טהורה, she is טהורה and the other two are טמאות. If two examined themselves and were found טהורות, they are טהורות and the third is טמאה. If all three were found טהורות, all of them are טמאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how a בדיקה after the blood is found changes who is טמאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clean בדיקה rules out that woman as the source, so the doubt moves onto the others. But the blood must have come from someone. If all three are found clean, the בדיקה cannot clear anyone, and all three stay טמאות.
steps.confusionAlert: It sounds strange that three clean examinations make everyone טמאה. The point is that the blood came from one of them, so a clean result cannot clear all three.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the rule: a בדיקה can move the doubt from one woman to another, but it cannot make the blood disappear.

phrases.english: If one of them examined herself and was found pure —
she is pure, and the two are impure.
If two examined themselves and found they were pure —
they are pure, and the third is impure.
If all three of them examined and found they were pure —
all of them are impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּדְקָה אַחַת מֵהֶן וְנִמְצֵאת טְהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds how a בדיקה affects the case laid out in steps 2–3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A clean בדיקה clears that woman and leaves the rest טמאות. If all three are found clean, all three are טמאות.

steps.title: Comparison to a mixed-up impure pile of stones
steps.stepSummary: The משנה compares the case to one טמא pile mixed up with two טהור piles. Checking piles clears them, and the doubt moves onto the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this like? A טמא pile that got mixed up among two טהור piles. They checked one of them and found it טהור: it is טהור, and the other two are טמאים. If they checked two and found them טהורים, they are טהורים and the third is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a comparison to explain the logic of the examinations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know one pile has something טמא under it, but we don't know which. Each pile that is checked and found clean is cleared, and the טומאה is pinned on the piles that are left. The women work the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this like? It introduces a comparison

steps.whatToRemember: Blood under one woman makes her and her neighbor טמאות (all three if it is in the middle, or if they crossed over the bed). A clean בדיקה clears a woman and moves the doubt onto the others, like checking mixed-up piles. If all three are found clean, all stay טמאות.

phrases.english: To what is the matter comparable?
To an impure pile that became intermingled
phrases.notes: A pile of stones with a piece of a dead body underneath it, which makes it טמא.

phrases.english: among two pure piles,
and they examined one of them and found it pure —
it is pure, and the two are impure.
If they examined two and found them pure —
they are pure, and the third is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה הַדָּבָר דוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a comparison that explains the examination rules of step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Like mixed-up piles, each item checked and found clean is cleared, and the טומאה rests on whatever has not been cleared.

steps.title: All three piles checked clean: רבי מאיר says all stay טמא
steps.stepSummary: If all three piles are searched and nothing is found, רבי מאיר rules that all of them are still טמא. Something with a חזקת טומאה stays טמא until you find where the טומאה is.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they checked all three piles and found them clean, all of them are טמא. These are the words of רבי מאיר, because רבי מאיר says: anything that has a status of טומאה stays טמא forever, until you know where the טומאה is.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the pile-of-stones comparison. It rules that if all three piles are checked and found clean, all three stay טמא, and it gives רבי מאיר's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know for sure that the טומאה is in one of the piles. Not finding it does not remove it, so רבי מאיר assumes the search simply was not good enough. This matches the women's case, where all three stay טמאות if all three are found clean.

keyTerms.meaning: An established status of being טמא
It stays in its טומאה forever
Until it becomes known to you

steps.whyThisMatters: This is רבי מאיר's general rule: a known טומאה does not go away just because you could not find it. It explains why the three women all stay טמאות when all three check and are clean.

phrases.english: [If they checked] all three, and found them clean —
phrases.notes: This sentence started just before this point. It is talking about checking all three piles of stones.

phrases.english: all of them are impure; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
For Rabbi Meir says:
anything that has the status of impurity —
forever remains in its impurity,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיִּוָּדַע לְךָ טוּמְאָה הֵיכָן הִיא.
phrases.english: until it becomes known to you where the impurity is.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלָּן טְמֵאִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. שֶׁרַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the pile comparison from Step 5 and gives רבי מאיר's reason
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If all three piles are found clean, all stay טמא, because a known טומאה stays until it is located.

steps.title: The חכמים say to dig down to bedrock or untouched soil
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. You search until you reach bedrock or soil that was never dug. If nothing is found, it is clean.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: he searches until he reaches bedrock or untouched soil.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר about the piles. They say a full search, all the way down to rock or untouched ground, is enough to clear the pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Below bedrock or untouched soil there can be no buried טומאה. So if a full search finds nothing, we assume the טומאה was moved away, and the pile is clean. For the חכמים, a full enough search really does remove the doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Untouched soil that was never dug

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: a known טומאה stays until it is found. חכמים: search down to rock or untouched soil, and if nothing is there, it is clean.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹדֵק עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְסֶלַע אוֹ לִבְתוּלָה.
phrases.english: he searches until he reaches bedrock or virgin soil.
phrases.notes: "Virgin soil" means ground nobody ever dug, so nothing could be buried below it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opinion that argues with רבי מאיר in Step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Search until bedrock or untouched soil; if nothing is found, the pile is clean.

steps.title: Why does one משנה split by location and the other does not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the earlier משנה made all three women טמאות wherever the blood was found. Our משנה splits based on where the blood was. What is the difference?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is different about the first case, which does not make a split, and what is different about the later case, which does make a split?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by pointing out a contrast between two משניות about women sharing a bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה said that blood found under any of the women makes all three טמאות. Our משנה says it depends on whether the blood was under the middle woman or an end woman. Both seem to be the same case, so why are the rulings different?

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the אמוראים on the משנה
The first part or earlier case
The later part or later case

steps.confusionAlert: Here "רישא" does not mean the first line of our משנה. It means the earlier משנה about the women, and "סיפא" is our משנה.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is different about the first case, which does not distinguish,
phrases.notes: The "first case" is the earlier משנה, where blood under any one woman made all three טמאות.

phrases.english: and what is different about the latter case, which does distinguish?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא דְּלָא מְפַלֵּיג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by comparing our משנה to the earlier one
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between the earlier משנה (all three טמאות) and our משנה (it depends on location)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two cases look the same, so the different rulings need an explanation.

steps.title: רבי אמי: the earlier case is about women lying intertwined
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that the earlier משנה is talking about women whose bodies were tangled together. Then nobody has a clear place in the bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: it is talking about women who were intertwined.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers the question by explaining that the earlier משנה is a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the women are tangled together, you cannot say who was in the middle and who was on the end. So the location of the blood tells us nothing, and all three are טמאות. Our משנה is about women lying in clear, separate places, so location does matter.
steps.whatToRemember: The earlier משנה is about intertwined women, so all three are טמאות. Our משנה is about women in fixed places, so it depends on where the blood was found.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
[It is talking] about women who were intertwined.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: בִּמְשׁוּלָּבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contrast raised in Step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות are about the same situation, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The earlier משנה is about intertwined women, where location cannot be known, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Why did the משנה need the comparison 'what is this like'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the part of the משנה about one woman checking herself. It asks why the משנה added the comparison to piles of stones at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if one of them checked herself, and so on. Why does it need to teach 'what is this like'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה and asks why the pile-of-stones comparison was needed. This sets up an answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rulings about the women checking themselves seem clear on their own. So the comparison to the piles looks like extra words. The גמרא wants to know what new thing the comparison teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this like? The משנה's phrase for bringing a comparison
And so on. It shows the quote continues

phrases.english: If one of them examined herself, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה from Step 4. "Etc." just means the rest of that line.

phrases.english: Why does he need to teach "To what is this comparable"?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לֵיהּ לְמִתְנֵי לְמָה זֶה דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about a different line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the comparison to the piles of stones adds beyond the rulings about the women

steps.title: רבי מאיר uses the blood case to push the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: The comparison to the piles is really רבי מאיר arguing with the רבנן: why do you agree with me about the blood but not about the piles?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי מאיר is telling the רבנן: what is different about the blood case, where you do not argue with me, and what is different about the pile case, where you do argue with me?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question from step 10. The comparison to the piles is רבי מאיר's argument against the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the blood case everyone agrees all three women stay טמאות even though only one of them really is. רבי מאיר says the piles are the same: something was there for sure, so all the piles should stay טמא even after a search. He uses the case the רבנן agree to as leverage against them.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? A way of asking why two cases are treated differently
A pile of stones (here, one of the three piles where טומאה may be buried)

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְרַבָּנַן:
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Meir is saying to the Rabbis:
What is different about blood, where you do not disagree,
and what is different about a pile, where you do disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10's question about why the משנה brought the comparison to the piles.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה mentions the piles of stones at all.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison is רבי מאיר's argument: since the רבנן agree the women are all טמאות, they should agree the piles are all טמא too.

steps.title: The Rabbis explain why blood is different from a pile
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that the טומאה in a pile could have been carried away by a raven, but the blood had to come from one of the women.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: it makes sense there, by the piles, since you can say a raven took the טומאה away. But here, where did this blood come from?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן defend themselves against רבי מאיר. They show why the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the pile case, the טומאה might simply be gone, for example a bird carried it off, so after a search all the piles can be clean. In the blood case the blood is right there in front of us, so it surely came from one of the women. That is why they keep all three טמאות.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (introduces the case that works, before the case that doesn't)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר says a sure טומאה keeps all the piles טמא. The רבנן say a pile is different from blood, because the טומאה in a pile may have been taken away, while blood has to come from one of the women.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis [would say]:
It makes sense there,
say a raven took it,
but here,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the three women and the blood.

phrases.english: this blood, where did it come from?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, בִּשְׁלָמָא הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי מאיר's argument from step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The blood case and the pile case are the same, so they should have the same ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a pile the טומאה may have been taken away, but blood must have come from one of the women.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's story of the sycamore tree in כפר סבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר tells of a tree people thought had טומאה under it. They searched and found nothing, but later a skull was found in its roots.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר said, there was a story with a sycamore tree in כפר סבא that people believed had טומאה under it. They searched and found nothing. Some time later, the wind blew and uprooted the tree, and a skull of a dead person was found stuck in its roots.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר brings a story to prove his view. A search can miss the טומאה, so a search cannot make the place clean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up רבי מאיר's rule from step 6: a place with a חזקת טומאה stays טמא even if a search finds nothing. The story shows a real case where the search failed and the טומאה really was there.

keyTerms.meaning: A story that really happened, brought as a proof
People believed there was טומאה there (it had a חזקת טומאה)

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Meir said:
There was an incident with a sycamore of Kefar Sava,
which they presumed had טומאה,
and they searched and did not find [anything].
Some days later the wind blew on it and uprooted it,
and a skull of a dead person was found
stuck in its roots.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּשִׁקְמָה שֶׁל כְּפַר סָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to stories that support רבי מאיר's view that a search is not trustworthy.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's view that a place with a חזקת טומאה stays טמא even after a search finds nothing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the sycamore in כפר סבא, where a skull was found after a failed search.

steps.title: The Sages reject the sycamore proof
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the story proves nothing: maybe they did not search well enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is that a proof? Say that they did not search as much as they needed to.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי מאיר's story. They say the search itself was not done properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים never said any search works. In step 7 they said you must search all the way down to untouched ground. A skull showing up later only shows that this search was too weak. It does not show that a proper search can't be trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof? (meaning: you can't prove anything from there)

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not denying that the skull was there. They only deny that the story proves a proper search can fail.

phrases.english: They said to him: Is that a proof?
Say that they did not search as much as necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the sycamore story only, not the facts of the story.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story may show a poor search, not that a proper search fails.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's story of the cave in שיחין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי tells of a cave people thought had טומאה. They searched down to smooth ground and found nothing, but later workers dug and found a mortar full of bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי said, there was a story with a cave in שיחין that people believed had טומאה. They searched until they reached ground as smooth as a fingernail and found nothing. Some time later, workers went in to get out of the rain, dug with their axes, and found a mortar full of bones.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story is brought to prove that a search can miss the טומאה. This time the search seemed very thorough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story is stronger than the first one. They searched until the ground looked smooth and untouched, which sounds like the full search the חכמים asked for in step 7. Even so, bones were found later.

keyTerms.meaning: Smooth as a fingernail (ground that looks like it was never dug)

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yosei said:
There was an incident with a cave of Shichin,
which they presumed had טומאה,
and they searched until they reached ground
that was smooth as a fingernail, and they did not find [anything].

phrases.aramaic: לְיָמִים נִכְנְסוּ בָּהּ פּוֹעֲלִים מִפְּנֵי הַגְּשָׁמִים,
phrases.english: Some days later workers went into it because of the rain,
and they struck [the ground] with their axes,
and they found a mortar full of bones.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מַעֲשֶׂה בִּמְעָרָה שֶׁל שִׁיחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second, stronger story of a failed search.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that even a thorough search can miss hidden טומאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the cave in שיחין, where bones were found after a search down to smooth ground.

steps.title: The Sages reject the cave proof too
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים give the same answer: maybe even this search was not done well enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is that a proof? Say that they did not search as much as they needed to.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject the second story with the very same words they used for the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the ground looked smooth, the חכמים say the search still was not complete. So the story only shows a weak search. Both stories end without proving that a proper search fails, and the חכמים' view from step 7 stays standing.
steps.whatToRemember: Two stories try to show a search can miss טומאה. Both times the חכמים answer the same way: the search was not done well enough. So a proper search can still be trusted, as they said in step 7.

phrases.english: They said to him: Is that a proof?
Say that they did not search as much as necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 15 the same way step 14 rejected step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the cave story.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Even a search down to smooth ground may not have been complete.

steps.title: The rock at בית חורון and the wet sheets
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול tells of a large rock area thought to hide טומאה. רבי יהושע בן חנניה spread wet sheets over it and found a big pit full of bones.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול said: There was a rock at בית חורון that people thought had טומאה. The חכמים could not check it because it was too big. An old man named רבי יהושע בן חנניה asked for sheets. He soaked them in water and spread them out. Where it was pure, the sheet dried. Where there was טומאה, it stayed wet. They dug there and found a big pit full of bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more story about a place people suspected had טומאה. This time a clever way of checking actually found the bones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 13–16, searches failed and the bones were found only later. Here the area was too large for a normal search, so רבי יהושע בן חנניה used a smarter test, and it worked. The story shows that hidden טומאה can really be there even when nobody can see it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rock, here a large area of rocky ground
People assumed the place had טומאה

phrases.english: It was taught: Abba Shaul says:
There was an incident with the rock of Beit Choron,
which people assumed had corpse impurity in it,
and the Sages could not check it
because it was too large.
And there was one old man there,
and his name was Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya.
He said to them: Bring me sheets!
They brought him sheets,
and he soaked them in water and spread them over it.
phrases.notes: "Over them" means over the whole rocky area they were checking.

phrases.english: The pure places were dry,
the places of impurity were wet,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָדְקוּ וּמָצְאוּ בּוֹר גָּדוֹל מָלֵא עֲצָמוֹת.
phrases.english: and they checked and found a large pit full of bones.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּסֶלַע בֵּית חוֹרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third story about hidden טומאה. Unlike the earlier ones, here a clever search worked.
steps.raayaObject: Hidden טומאה can really exist even where no one can see it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story told by אבא שאול about the rock at בית חורון.

steps.title: This was the pit of ישמעאל בן נתניה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא identifies the pit as the one ישמעאל בן נתניה filled with dead bodies, and quotes the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: This was the pit that ישמעאל בן נתניה filled with dead people, as the פסוק says: "And the pit where ישמעאל threw all the bodies of the men he killed by the hand of גדליה."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us whose bones were in the pit and brings a פסוק as the source. This also sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pit is linked to a known event in תנ״ך. The words of the פסוק, "by the hand of גדליה," seem strange, and the גמרא will ask about them next.

phrases.english: It was taught: That is the pit
that Yishmael ben Netanya filled with slain people,
as it is written: "And the pit where Yishmael threw
all the bodies of the men
whom he struck by the hand of Gedalya."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 41:9. Keep the words "by the hand of" in mind, because the גמרא is about to ask about them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הוּא הַבּוֹר שֶׁמִּילֵּא יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן נְתַנְיָה חֲלָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the pit from the story in step 17 and brings a פסוק about it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pit at בית חורון is the pit ישמעאל בן נתניה filled with the people he killed.

steps.title: Did גדליה kill them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק says the killing was "by the hand of גדליה" when ישמעאל was the killer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did גדליה kill them? But ישמעאל killed them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the פסוק. It seems to blame גדליה for murders that ישמעאל did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "by the hand of גדליה" sound like גדליה did the killing. But ישמעאל was the murderer, and גדליה was one of his victims. So why does the פסוק link the deaths to גדליה?

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really so that...? (a word that opens a challenge)

phrases.english: And did Gedalya kill them?
But didn't Yishmael kill them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי גְדַלְיָה הֲרָגָן? וַהֲלֹא יִשְׁמָעֵאל הֲרָגָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the פסוק quoted in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase "בְּיַד גְּדַלְיָה" in the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The facts are that ישמעאל did the killing, so blaming גדליה seems wrong.

steps.title: גדליה ignored the warning
steps.stepSummary: Because גדליה should have taken the warning of יוחנן בן קרח seriously and did not, the פסוק treats him as if he killed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, because he should have worried about the warning of יוחנן בן קרח and he did not worry, the פסוק counts it against him as if he had killed them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. גדליה is blamed because he ignored a warning that could have prevented the killings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גדליה did not kill anyone with his own hands. But he was warned about ישמעאל and did nothing, so the פסוק holds him responsible for the deaths. Not taking care to stop a danger you were warned about counts as real blame.

keyTerms.meaning: To be concerned, to take precautions
The פסוק counts it against him

steps.whatToRemember: A person who ignores a real warning can be held responsible for the harm that follows.

phrases.english: Rather, since he should have been concerned
about the advice of Yochanan ben Kareach,
phrases.notes: יוחנן בן קרח warned גדליה that ישמעאל was planning to kill him (ירמיהו 40:13–16).

phrases.english: and he was not concerned —
the verse counts it against him as if he killed them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ לָחוֹשׁ לַעֲצַת יוֹחָנָן בֶּן קָרֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the פסוק: blame for neglect, not for the act itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to say גדליה actually did the killing.
steps.terutzMaskana: גדליה is blamed as if he killed them because he ignored the warning.

steps.title: רבא: Don't believe לשון הרע, but be careful
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that you should not accept לשון הרע as true, but you must still take precautions because of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: About לשון הרע, even though you should not accept it as true, you do need to be careful because of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא learns a practical rule from the story of גדליה. You do not believe the bad report, but you still protect yourself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גדליה thought that refusing to listen to לשון הרע meant ignoring the warning completely. רבא makes a split: believing the report and acting against the person is forbidden, but taking precautions is required. That is why גדליה was blamed.

keyTerms.meaning: To be concerned, to take precautions

steps.whatToRemember: With לשון הרע: do not believe it (לקבולי), but do be careful because of it (מיחש).
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not allowing you to believe לשון הרע. He only says you must take care to protect yourself, without deciding that the report is true.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key practical rule for how to deal with warnings that sound like gossip.

phrases.english: Rava said: This evil speech,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי דִּלְקַבּוֹלֵי לָא מִבְּעֵי —
phrases.english: even though one should not accept it —
one should be concerned about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי לִישָּׁנָא בִּישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from גדליה's mistake in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not accept לשון הרע as true, but one must take precautions because of it.

steps.title: רבי טרפון refuses to hide the rumored killers
steps.stepSummary: People of the Galilee who were rumored to have killed someone asked רבי טרפון to hide them. He told them to hide themselves, because the Rabbis taught that even though you should not believe לשון הרע, you must still take precautions because of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people from the Galilee were rumored to have killed someone. They came to רבי טרפון and asked him to hide them. He said: What should I do? If I don't hide you, they will find you. But if I do hide you, the Rabbis taught that even though you shouldn't accept לשון הרע as true, you must still be careful because of it. So go and hide yourselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows רבא's rule from step 21 being used in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון is stuck in the middle. If he refuses, the people might be caught. But the rumor that they are killers is something he has to take seriously, so he cannot shelter them himself. His answer follows the rule exactly. He does not treat them as guilty, since he lets them go and hide. But he protects himself by not hiding them in his own place.

keyTerms.meaning: Evil speech (לשון הרע), meaning a negative report about someone
One must be concerned about it and take precautions

steps.whatToRemember: Not believing a rumor and being careful because of it are two different things. רבי טרפון did both at once.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי טרפון is not saying the people are guilty. He does not turn them in. He tells them to hide themselves. He only refuses to be the one hiding them.

phrases.english: There were these people of the Galilee
about whom a rumor went out that they had killed a person.
They came before Rabbi Tarfon
and said to him: Will the Master hide us?
He said to them: What should we do?
If I do not hide you, they will see you.
If I do hide you,
didn't the Rabbis say:
phrases.notes: This is the same rule רבא taught in step 21.

phrases.english: This evil speech,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּלְקַבּוֹלֵי לָא מִבְּעֵי —
phrases.english: even though one should not accept it as true,
one must be concerned about it.
You go and hide yourselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ בְּנֵי גָּלִילָא דִּנְפַק עֲלַיְיהוּ קָלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that shows רבא's rule (step 21) being applied in practice
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that you must take precautions because of לשון הרע even though you may not believe it
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רבי טרפון in the story of the people of the Galilee

steps.title: Why was משה told not to fear עוג but not סיחון?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק tells משה 'do not fear' עוג. סיחון and עוג were brothers, so why would משה fear one and not the other?
steps.simpleTranslation: ה׳ said to משה: 'Do not fear him' (about עוג). But סיחון and עוג were brothers, sons of אחיה son of שמחזאי. So what made עוג different, that משה was afraid of him, and what made סיחון different, that he was not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new פסוק about the war with עוג. It asks a question about it, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the war with סיחון, ה׳ never had to calm משה down. Before the war with עוג, He did. Since the two kings were brothers from the same family, family strength cannot explain the difference. So something else must have made משה afraid of עוג.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, after all (opens a point the question is built on)

phrases.english: "And the Lord said to Moses: Do not fear"
Now, Sichon and Og were brothers,
as the Master said:

phrases.aramaic: סִיחוֹן וְעוֹג בְּנֵי אֲחִיָּה בַּר שַׁמְחֲזַאי הֲווֹ,
phrases.english: Sichon and Og were sons of Achiyah son of Shamchazai.
What is different about Og, that he was afraid,
phrases.notes: 'He' is משה, who was afraid of עוג.

phrases.english: and what is different about Sichon, that he was not afraid?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא מֵעוֹג דְּקָמִסְתְּפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new פסוק and asks a question about it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why משה feared עוג but not his brother סיחון

steps.title: משה feared אברהם's merit would protect עוג
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי, says that ה׳'s answer shows what משה was thinking. He worried that the זכות of אברהם אבינו would protect עוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: From the answer given to that צדיק, you can tell what was in his heart. He said: Maybe the זכות of אברהם אבינו will stand up for עוג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 23. משה was afraid that עוג had a special merit from אברהם protecting him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was not afraid of עוג's strength. He feared that עוג had earned protection from אברהם's merit. סיחון had no such merit, so there was nothing to fear from him. ה׳'s words 'do not fear' were reassuring משה about this exact worry.

keyTerms.meaning: His answer, here meaning the answer ה׳ gave to משה
Righteous person, here referring to משה
Merit, a good deed that can protect a person

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said that Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said:
From the answer given to that righteous one,
phrases.notes: The righteous one is משה, and the answer is ה׳ telling him 'do not fear.'

phrases.english: you know what was in his heart.
He said: Perhaps there will stand for him
the merit of Abraham our father.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִתְּשׁוּבָתוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ מָה הָיָה בְּלִבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה feared that עוג would be protected by the זכות of אברהם אבינו

steps.title: עוג was the escapee who brought אברהם the news
steps.stepSummary: The source for עוג's connection to אברהם is the פסוק 'the escapee came and told אברם העברי.' רבי יוחנן says this escapee was עוג, who survived the generation of the flood.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'The escapee came and told אברם העברי.' And רבי יוחנן said: This is עוג, who escaped from the generation of the flood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to show why עוג had a connection to אברהם's merit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, someone escapes the war and tells אברהם that his relative was captured, so אברהם can go and rescue him. רבי יוחנן identifies this escapee as עוג. He is called 'the escapee' because he survived the flood. Since עוג did אברהם this favor, משה worried it had earned him protection.

keyTerms.meaning: The escapee, the one who got away
Avram the Ivri, אברהם before his name was changed
The generation of the flood in the time of נח

steps.whatToRemember: משה feared עוג and not סיחון because עוג had once helped אברהם by bringing him news. That gave him a merit that might protect him.

phrases.english: As it is stated: "And the escapee came
and told Abram the Hebrew,"
And Rabbi Yochanan said: This is Og,
who escaped from the generation of the flood.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיָּבֹא הַפָּלִיט וַיַּגֵּד לְאַבְרָם הָעִבְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source showing why עוג had a connection to אברהם's merit
steps.raayaObject: That עוג had a merit tied to אברהם אבינו
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 14:13, together with רבי יוחנן's teaching that the escapee was עוג

steps.title: Cleaning a garment whose stain was lost
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a כתם on a garment can no longer be found, you scrub the garment with seven cleaning substances, and the stain is cancelled. Then רבי שמעון בן אלעזר starts to give his own opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If a garment had a blood stain, and now you cannot find the stain, you scrub the whole garment with seven cleaning substances, and that cancels the stain. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new rule: a garment whose stain was lost becomes fine again once you scrub it with seven cleaning substances. The last line names רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, which sets up his own view in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is that the stain is still there in our minds, but we cannot find it anymore. Since we do not know which spot to wash, the ברייתא says to use all seven cleaning substances on the garment. This counts as getting rid of the stain, even though no one ever saw it go away. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is about to add his own opinion on this case.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood stain found on a garment, which can make it טמא
A garment that had a stain, but now you cannot find where the stain is
Seven cleaning substances that are used to remove blood stains
He cancels it, meaning the stain no longer counts

steps.confusionAlert: "Lost" does not mean the garment was lost. The garment is right here. It is the stain on it that can no longer be found.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A garment on which a stain was lost,
phrases.notes: The stain was there before, but now you just can't tell where on the garment it is.

phrases.english: one passes seven substances over it
and cancels it.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בֶּגֶד שֶׁאָבַד בּוֹ כֶּתֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story about עוג and goes back to the halachic theme of steps 5–7: טומאה that is known to exist but can no longer be found. Here it is a stain that can no longer be located on a garment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A garment whose כתם can no longer be found is made fine again by scrubbing it with seven cleaning substances, which cancels the stain. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר then begins to give his own opinion.
